title: Manhattan Clinic - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
topics: Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
summary: Kickoff call for Manhattan Clinic onboarding. Redwood AE/CSM/SE introduced the onboarding plan and timelines. Customer described current infra (GCP with VPCs, strict data residency in US-east), compliance needs (SOC 2, encryption at rest, strict RBAC). Team discussed deployment options; customer leaning towards Private (VPC) with eventual Dedicated reservation for throughput. Action items assigned for pricing, security docs, and a technical deep dive and benchmark run. Next steps: share SSO/SAML guide, security artifacts, schedule SE-led deep dive, and provision a trial Dedicated cluster for benchmarking.

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-10-14
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood CSM), Evan Liu (Redwood SE); Dr. Rachel Green, Michael Torres, Amira Hassan, Samir Patel (Manhattan Clinic)

Summary / Notes (auto): Onboarding kickoff	6 focus on private deployment (VPC) due to PHI-equivalent dataset constraints, discuss SSO/SAML, KMS, SOC2, Dedicated throughput for 99th percentile latency.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood. We'll do quick intros then go over the onboarding plan. How's everyone?
[00:07] Dr. Rachel Green: Hi Alex, Rachel here. We're excited to get started, thanks for working with us.
[00:11] Michael Torres: Michael from Manhattan engineering. Quick note - we have strict data residency and most of our traffic is east coast US.
[00:17] Alex Kim: Great, noted. I'll hand over to Priya to walk the onboarding milestones.
[00:21] Priya Shah: Hi all, Priya - I'll be the CSM. High level: two-week pilot, security review, then production cutover timeline. We'll need sample workloads, success criteria. Questions up front?
[00:34] Amira Hassan: From compliance - we need SOC 2 type II, encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integration ideally customer-managed, and audit logs for all model calls.
[00:43] Evan Liu: Yep, we support customer KMS and audit logging. For Private deployments we can arrange customer-managed key material and HSM integrations, plus RBAC. Small caveat, some providers use different names, so we'll send a detailed doc.
[00:55] Samir Patel: Is VPC peering supported with GCP? We use GCP and have multiple VPCs.
[00:59] Evan Liu: Yes, we do VPC peering and private endpoints. For on-prem/air-gapped there's a different flow, but for your GCP we can do VPC peering and private connectivity. Might require firewall rules and IP allow-list.
[01:10] Michael Torres: Ok, and latency - our target is sub-250ms p50 for short prompts, and throughput around 200 reqs/sec for peak during business hours. Does that map to Redwood Dedicated?
[01:20] Alex Kim: Likely Dedicated for steady throughput, Private (VPC) deployment for data residency - you can have both: a private control plane with customer-managed network, and dedicated GPU pools for predictable throughput. We'll propose a config.
[01:32] Michael Torres: Any alternatives? We wanna balance cost.
[01:35] Priya Shah: There's also hosted with strict contractual terms, but given PHI-ish constraints you probably want Private. We can run a cost/latency comparison - Redwood Optimize has guidance for quantization/batching to reduce unit costs.
[01:50] Dr. Rachel Green: We also need to confirm model governance. Do you keep model versions, and can we pin a version to avoid surprise regressions?
[01:56] Evan Liu: Yes, model pinning and rollout policies are first-class. We also offer automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants if capacity is constrained, but that can be disabled for compliance-sensitive use.
[02:08] Amira Hassan: On audit logs - how long do you retain logs by default and can we export for our SIEM?
[02:13] Priya Shah: Default retention is 90 days on the hosted plane, but for Private we can configure retention and exports to your SIEM or S3. We'll share the exact options.
[02:25] Alex Kim: Quick clarification - does the team want a SE-led technical deep dive and a performance benchmark run as part of pilot?
[02:30] Michael Torres: Yes, definitely. We want to run customer traffic against a dedicated instance.
[02:34] Evan Liu: Cool - I'll put together a benchmark plan. We'll need a sample traffic CSV, typical prompt lengths, concurrency distribution. If you have examples of peak vs off-peak that helps tune batching and KV cache.
[02:47] Samir Patel: KV cache - sorry sometimes I hear KV cash - how do you handle long context?
[02:52] Evan Liu: Ha yes - K-V cache, it's the key-value attention cache. We support prefix caching and chunked KV for long contexts; that'll reduce token cost and latency for repeated prompts. We'll show real numbers in the benchmark.
[03:05] Michael Torres: Security question - SSO, we use Okta, SAML. Can we do SSO into Redwood Console and restrict via RBAC?
[03:12] Priya Shah: Absolutely. We support SAML/Okta and can set RBAC roles. We'll send SSO guide and a checklist for the identity team.
[03:20] Amira Hassan: About encryption - we need CMEK integration for keys so that only our key can decrypt model payloads at rest.
[03:27] Evan Liu: We support CMEK for Private deployments; for Hosted we'd need contractual controls and customer-managed key wrapping in some regions. We'll detail options.
[03:36] Dr. Rachel Green: Great. On timeline, we aim to be in pilot within two weeks. Is that realistic?
[03:42] Alex Kim: Two weeks is tight but doable if we get sample traffic and IP allow list today, and we provision a trial Dedicated cluster. We'll try to provision by 2027-10-21.
[03:52] Michael Torres: And pricing?
[03:54] Alex Kim: I'll send a pricing sheet. For Dedicated there are reserved capacity commitments; for the pilot we can offer short-term trial pricing and show unit costs. Priya will include Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization to reduce costs.
[04:08] Priya Shah: I'll also include a short onboarding checklist with dates and owners.
[04:12] Amira Hassan: One more - any third-party penetration test or SOC attestations you can share?
[04:18] Priya Shah: Yes, SOC2 Type II report, ISO certs, and our pen-test summary can be shared under NDA. I'll attach them.
[04:27] Alex Kim: Ok, next steps recap: Alex shares deck + pricing + SSO guide; Priya shares security package; Evan schedules deep dive and benchmarking; Manhattan provides traffic and IP ranges.
[04:40] Michael Torres: Sounds good. I'll get the traffic profile and ranges by Tuesday.
[04:44] Dr. Rachel Green: We'll review docs and get compliance questions back to you.
[04:48] Alex Kim: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[04:52] Priya Shah: Thanks all, expect emails from Alex and me with attachments.
[04:55] Evan Liu: I'll send a Doodle for the deep dive slots, thanks.
[04:58] Amira Hassan: Thanks, bye.
[04:59] Alex Kim: Bye everyone.

End of transcript.
